question: Which component(s) of blood is/are mainly responsible for transporting food, carbon dioxide and nitrogenous wastes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood** is a connective tissue in fluid form that consists of a fluid medium called **plasma** in which various cells are suspended.
 
• **Plasma** is primarily responsible for the transport of **food** (nutrients like glucose, amino acids, and lipids), **carbon dioxide**, and **nitrogenous wastes** (such as urea) in a dissolved form throughout the body. ***Hence, the correct answer is Plasma.***
 
• It constitutes about **55%** of the total blood volume and is composed of nearly **90-92% water**, with the remaining **8-10%** consisting of proteins, mineral salts, hormones, and waste products.
 
• While **Red Blood Corpuscles (RBCs)** primarily transport **oxygen** using **hemoglobin**, **plasma** carries **carbon dioxide** more efficiently as it is more soluble in water and is often transported in the form of **bicarbonate ions**.
 
• The process of transporting **nitrogenous waste** involves **plasma** carrying substances like **urea** from the **liver** to the **kidneys** for excretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Red Blood Corpuscles (Erythrocytes):**
 
 
• These are **biconcave** cells that lack a **nucleus** in most mammals to provide more space for **hemoglobin**.
 
• Their primary function is to transport **oxygen** from the lungs to all body tissues and a small amount of **carbon dioxide** back to the lungs.
 
• The average lifespan of an **RBC** is approximately **120 days**, after which they are destroyed in the **spleen**.
 
 
 
• **White Blood Cells (Leukocytes):**
 
 
• These cells act as the body’s **immune system** and help fight against **infections** and foreign particles.
 
• They are divided into **Granulocytes** (Neutrophils, Eosinophils, Basophils) and **Agranulocytes** (Lymphocytes, Monocytes).
 
• They are much fewer in number compared to **RBCs** but can increase rapidly during an **infection** or **inflammation**.
 
 
 
• **Platelets (Thrombocytes):**
 
 
• These are tiny, **cell fragments** produced in the **bone marrow** from **megakaryocytes**.
 
• Their main function is to help in **blood clotting** (coagulation) to prevent excessive bleeding when a blood vessel is injured.
 
• A low count of **platelets** can lead to excessive bleeding, a condition known as **thrombocytopenia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plasma Proteins:**
 
 
• **Fibrinogen**: Essential for **blood clotting** or coagulation.
 
• **Globulins**: Primarily involved in the **defense mechanisms** of the body (immunoglobulins).
 
• **Albumins**: Help in maintaining the **osmotic balance** of the blood.
 
 
 
• **Transport Mechanism:** 
 
 
• Nutrients absorbed from the **digestive tract**, such as **glucose** and **fatty acids**, are dissolved in the **plasma** and distributed to cells.
 
• The **pH level** of blood is maintained around **7.4**, which is slightly **alkaline**, largely due to the buffering capacity of **plasma** components.
 
• **Hormones** secreted by **endocrine glands** are also transported via **plasma** to their respective target organs.
